tagline: Up the Okanogan River from the Columbia to Canada.
intro: US 97 leaves Pateros at the mouth of the Methow and continues northeast to Brewster, then turns north up the east bank of the Okanogan River, inside the Colville Reservation, around Soap Lake Mountain and past Malott. It bypasses Okanogan and Omak, crosses the river, and keeps company with it on through Riverside and Tonasket to Oroville, then runs along the west side of Osoyoos Lake to the border.
The road north from Pateros joined the state system in 1905 and was carried to the border in 1907, as part of the Wenatchee-Oroville Road.
season: State of Washington Tourism names spring through fall as the best conditions for outdoor recreation and wildlife viewing.

moments.title: Fort Okanogan
moments.text: John Jacob Astor's Pacific Fur Company built its post here in 1811 where the Okanogan meets the Columbia, and since 1967 the site has lain under Lake Pateros, behind Wells Dam.

moments.title: Omak
moments.text: On the second weekend of August, riders in the Stampede's Suicide Race take their horses down a 62-degree slope and into the Okanogan River, once the horses have passed a swim test.

moments.title: Oroville
moments.text: Named Oro for the nearby gold mines in 1892, the town became Oroville in 1909 because the post office already had an Oso and objected.
